concepts.name: Insolation and heat balance
concepts.mechanism: Insolation is incoming solar radiation. Solar angle, day length, clouds and surface reflectivity affect absorbed energy. Earth reflects some incoming energy and emits longwave radiation; radiation, convection and latent heat help redistribute energy. The greenhouse effect is distinct from ozone depletion.
concepts.example: Dark and bright surfaces can absorb different fractions of the same sunlight. Cloud and atmosphere also modify the energy reaching and leaving the surface.
concepts.mistake: Incoming radiation is not all absorbed, and greenhouse warming is not the same mechanism as an ozone hole.
items: If reflectivity increases while incoming sunlight is unchanged, what generally happens to absorbed sunlight?
Two roofs receive similar sunlight; one reflects a larger fraction. What can be inferred before considering other heat flows?
It absorbs less of that incoming radiation
It must have identical temperature at every moment
It has removed the greenhouse effect

concepts.name: Pressure gradients and winds
concepts.mechanism: Air motion responds to pressure-gradient force and is modified by Earth's rotation, friction and curvature. Unequal heating can help create pressure differences, but winds are not explained by temperature alone. Circulation changes with scale, terrain and season.
concepts.example: Near a coast, different heating of land and sea can help produce a pressure contrast and a breeze. Local circulation also depends on surrounding conditions.
concepts.mistake: Wind is not simply a direct movement from every hot place to every cold place.
items: Which force initiates air motion in response to a pressure difference?
What modifies a wind driven by a pressure gradient?
Rotation and friction, among other influences
Why is a temperature-only wind explanation incomplete?
Pressure structure and other forces affect air motion
A coastal breeze differs between an open plain and a rough built-up coast. Which additional influence should be considered?
Only whether the map is flat
Only the name of the town

concepts.name: Humidity, cooling and condensation
concepts.mechanism: Relative humidity compares actual vapour pressure with saturation vapour pressure at the same temperature. Cooling can bring moist air to saturation. Clouds require suitable condensation or ice processes; precipitation also depends on lifting, stability and microphysics. Moisture alone does not guarantee rain.
concepts.example: Air can reach saturation as it cools without adding water vapour. Dew point describes the cooling needed under approximately constant pressure and moisture content.
concepts.mistake: High moisture by itself is not proof that rainfall will occur, and relative humidity is temperature-dependent.
items: Relative humidity is evaluated against saturation at—
Without adding vapour, what can bring air nearer saturation?
No; lifting, stability and cloud processes matter
Yes, every humid day must rain
No, moisture is irrelevant to clouds
Two equally moist air masses have different temperatures and stability. Must their rain outcomes match?
No; saturation and lifting conditions may differ
Yes; water amount is the only factor

concepts.name: Orographic lifting and rain shadows
concepts.mechanism: Moist air encountering relief can rise, expand and cool toward saturation. Windward precipitation may increase; descending leeward air often warms and has lower relative humidity. Wind direction, moisture, stability and terrain control the effect; highest elevation is not automatically wettest.
concepts.example: Changing the prevailing moist wind from west to east can change which mountain slope is windward. Rainfall still depends on moisture and atmospheric conditions.
concepts.mistake: Altitude alone cannot identify a rain shadow or the wettest slope.
items: Which slope faces the incoming moist wind?
Why can leeward air become relatively drier?
Descending air warms, lowering relative humidity under suitable conditions
Moist prevailing wind reverses across a mountain range. What should you reconsider?
Which slope is windward, along with moisture and stability
